title: Vaccines That Protect You and Your Baby
hook: Certain vaccines in pregnancy do double duty: they protect you from serious illness and pass antibodies to your baby, shielding them in the early weeks before their own shots.
key_points: Recommended vaccines in pregnancy include Tdap (whooping cough), flu, and RSV — exact options depend on your country and season.
Antibodies cross the placenta, protecting your newborn before they're old enough for their own vaccines.
Tdap is usually given in the third trimester (about 27–36 weeks) to maximise antibody transfer to the baby.
The RSV vaccine is typically given later (around 32–36 weeks) during the RSV season.
content_html: Some of the most effective protection a newborn gets happens before they're even born. When you're vaccinated in pregnancy, your body makes antibodies that cross the placenta to your baby — giving them a shield against serious infections in the first weeks of life, before they're old enough for their own vaccines.
extra_html: The CDC recommends several vaccines in pregnancy, including Tdap (which protects against whooping cough), the flu vaccine, and the RSV vaccine; the exact recommendations depend on your country, your health, and the season. Timing matters: Tdap is generally given in the third trimester (about 27–36 weeks) to maximise antibody transfer, and the maternal RSV vaccine is typically given a little later (around 32–36 weeks) during RSV season. This is general information — your midwife or doctor will advise which vaccines are right for you and when to have them.

related.title: How Childhood Vaccines Work
related.hook: Vaccines train a child's immune system to recognize a disease in advance, so it can fight off the real thing — and they're scheduled to protect kids when they're most vulnerable.

related.title: Why Prenatal Visits Matter
related.hook: Regular checkups during pregnancy catch problems early — for many a typical schedule is monthly, then every two weeks, then weekly as the due date nears.

flashcards.prompt: How do vaccines given in pregnancy help protect a newborn?

choices.text: Antibodies cross the placenta, protecting the baby before their own vaccines
They make the baby immune for life from birth
They replace the need for any childhood vaccines

flashcards.explanation_html: Vaccinating in pregnancy allows passive antibody transfer across the placenta, giving newborns protection in the gap before their own shots.

flashcards.prompt: When is the Tdap (whooping cough) vaccine usually given in pregnancy?
flashcards.back_html: Usually in the third trimester, around 27–36 weeks, which maximises the antibodies passed to the baby for protection against whooping cough.
